purpose: Selection record for four-position paired scoring in attend, plus the rejected sixteen-output FP32 analogue

baseline.description: Merged oct-output FP32 remainder-row kernel from PR #61 with scalar attend score pass

candidate.description: attend's score pass processes four positions per iteration, sharing each query load; each position keeps its ascending-index dot accumulation order and in-order max updates. The exp/value passes are unchanged.

kernel_results.median_ratio_summary: Whole-attend timing across three fresh processes: ~0.79-0.84x at head-dim 64, ~0.66-0.78x at head-dim 128, lengths 33-2048. Zero allocations both paths.

generation_results.median_ratio_summary: Synthetic FP32 fixture, 64 paired trials x 3 processes: ~0.96-0.97x for 128-token decode, ~0.97-0.98x for 129/257-length prefill one-token, ~0.98-0.99x elsewhere. Every completion matched. Effect grows with context length; this fixture keeps positions short.

real_model.note: ~1.00x at ~130 positions: attention is a small share here; adopted as a bit-exact no-regression step that scales with context length.

rejected_hypothesis.name: Sixteen-output FP32 remainder-row sharing
rejected_hypothesis.finding: ~1.0-1.58x (slower) across decode shapes in one process; register pressure defeats the sharing win past eight accumulators. Oct stays the ceiling. Rejected; experiment kept in cmd/monolith/fp32_outputs16_test.go.

limitations: Single host; attention share grows with context so longer contexts should benefit more, but this is not yet measured on real models
Prefill path shares the same attend function and is covered by identical-output tests
